cases.prompt: A test, `test_checkout_applies_discount`, passes locally but fails on CI about 1 in 5 runs with an assertion that the cart total is the pre-discount amount. It exercises code that reads the active promotions from a shared in-memory cache, applies matching ones to the cart, and asserts the total. The suite runs tests in parallel. When it fails, re-running just that test passes. How would you find the root cause? Give your diagnosis.

Our API returns a 500 on the POST /orders endpoint for roughly 2% of requests, clustered in short bursts a few times an hour. The error log shows `connection pool exhausted` from the database client. Traffic is steady and well below peak. The endpoint does: validate -> begin transaction -> insert order -> call an external tax API -> commit. Diagnose the most likely root cause and what you'd check next.

Document the architecture of this system for a new engineer. It's a URL-shortener SaaS: a React SPA; an API gateway; a 'links' service (create/resolve short codes, writes to Postgres, caches hot codes in Redis); an 'analytics' service (consumes click events from a Kafka topic the links service publishes to, aggregates into ClickHouse); an auth service (JWT); and a nightly batch job that rolls up analytics. Deployed as containers on Kubernetes. Produce the architecture documentation.

Document how data flows through this system. A mobile app uploads a photo to a REST API; the API stores the file in object storage (S3) and writes a record to Postgres; it publishes an 'image.uploaded' event to a queue; a worker consumes the event, generates thumbnails, writes them back to S3, and updates the Postgres record; a CDN serves the images. Users can later request their images, which the API lists from Postgres and returns CDN URLs. Produce the data-flow documentation, including where state lives and the boundaries crossed.

A note-taking app has 40k users but flat growth and weak retention: people try it, take a few notes, and drift off within two weeks. Its charter is 'the fastest place to capture and find a thought.' Current features: fast capture, full-text search, tags, markdown. Where could the product go from here? Give me the strategic options to consider.

A B2B invoicing tool for freelancers has strong usage among its ~5k paying users but has plateaued: acquisition is expensive and expansion revenue is near zero (everyone's on the same $12/mo plan). The team is unsure whether to push upmarket, broaden the product, or double down on the core. Lay out the directions worth considering before we commit.

We're adding a feature that lets any authenticated user upload a profile avatar image. The browser POSTs the file to our API, which stores it in S3 and serves it back from a public CDN URL to all users who view that profile. Threat-model this feature before we build it.

We're adding an inbound webhook: a payment provider will POST payment-status events to a new public endpoint `/webhooks/payments`, and our handler updates the corresponding order's paid/unpaid status in our database. Threat-model this integration.
